definition: Implicit means understood or meant without being directly stated.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word implicit. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know implicit should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Neither roommate ever said it out loud, but there was an implicit agreement that whoever cooked dinner never had to wash the dishes.
A hinted idea is lightly suggested once and might easily be missed — fainter than an implicit one, whose meaning is genuinely built in even though it is never stated.
An ingrained assumption sits even deeper than an implicit one — buried so far down that people follow it without ever noticing it exists.

Unspoken means never said aloud, though both sides know it — an unspoken rivalry, an unspoken worry. It covers anything left in silence, however it arose. Implicit is more specific: the meaning is folded inside something that was expressed — a remark, a contract, an action — waiting to be read out of it.

Tacit describes agreement given silently: no discussion happens, and consent is shown by not objecting. Implicit meaning rides inside words or actions that did occur — a landlord's remark carrying an unstated expectation. When silence itself does the agreeing, the word is tacit; when a statement hints beyond itself, it is implicit.

Understood means accepted without ever being put into words — 'it's understood that you call if you'll be late.' It points to standing arrangements everyone already accepts. Implicit points instead to meaning carried inside a particular statement or act, which a listener must draw out. An understood rule simply exists; an implicit message gets read.

Implicit means understood or meant without being directly stated.
When the landlord remarked, 'Good tenants usually stay for years,' the message to the young couple was implicit: he expected them to choose the two-year lease rather than the six-month one.
The landlord never directly asked them to sign the longer lease — the expectation was folded into his remark and understood without being stated.
That unstated-but-understood quality is exactly what implicit means.
Implicit is common in SAT reading passages about arguments — an implicit assumption, an implicit bias, implicit trust.
Be careful: implicit does not mean 'obvious.' It means present but never directly stated; its direct opposite is explicit.

The exchange student spent her first month mapping rules nobody had handed her.
Her host father's cheerful 'We keep Sundays quiet' turned out to carry an implicit curfew, though no hour was ever named.
A raised eyebrow at the dinner table meant second helpings were for guests to decline.
None of this was written anywhere, and none of it was hidden either; the meaning sat inside remarks and gestures, waiting to be read.
By December she could hear what her hosts were saying underneath what they said, and the house had no more surprises for her.
